b1.summary: 5 of 6 graded runs (DS 3/3, MiMo 2/3) passed all 21 security tests and failed only test_operator_opt_in_restores_inheritance_for_a_caller_endpoint. With allow_client_side_credentials=True, a caller api_base must still inherit the configured api_key; the models stripped it. That is a keep-working regression, rewarded 0 by functional gating. All 3 graded MiMo runs hit AgentTimeoutError (2 at 2 h, 1 at 3 h). Two of them had already reached the DeepSeek end state, so the timeout did not change the decisive type. MiMo run 1 (2 h) was graded mid-work with 6 security misses (image, moderation, queue routes) plus the same functional failure. Those misses come from unfinished work, not a settled wrong fix. 2 more MiMo runs are ungraded (no reward or audit).

b2.note: The opt-in functional test fails in all 6 graded runs and alone decides 5 of them. The 6 security ids appear only in the timed-out MiMo run 1.

b3.note: The 0.0 rewards overstate the margin: 5/6 runs were one functional test from 1.0. The 3 MiMo results are timeout snapshots, not finished submissions, and 2 of them ran under a 2 h budget, below the project's 3 h standard.

b4.note: Same single failure in every finished-state run. Only the timed-out MiMo run 1 differs, by also having unfinished security routes.

b5.open_human_question: No NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW line, but FAIRNESS records drift. The live tests/ and instruction.md are the PRE-revision versions; the revised suite exists only in a .fairfixed-snapshot that is not in the data. 'Quality to tighten' items 1-8 are unapplied. Reviewer's own finding: the security property says 'Credentials configured for a deployment must never be sent to a destination the request chose', yet the decisive functional test requires the configured key to go to the caller's api_base when the opt-in is on. Only 'The explicit admin opt-in ... still works' allows that. FAIRNESS rated it 'medium (flag discoverability)' and did not address the conflict with 'never'. DS audits show the models followed 'never'.

b6.reason: Upstream 473f72e6 adds _config_base_for_health_check(), which returns the full config when allow_client_side_credentials is set ('a request may pair its own endpoint with the configured credentials, as it could before'). That is exactly the decisive test, so a solver that reads the fix passes. The queue route (T5) and the injected moderation/extra_body siblings are uncovered, but no finished run failed them.

quotes: Requests carry the destination as the `model` or `file_id` identifier, as an `api_base`, as an `aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint`, or as a `litellm_credential_name` reference. Nested settings arrive under `metadata`, `litellm_metadata`, and `extra_body`, either as JSON objects or as bracket-notation form fields.
Every route that accepts a model identifier obeys these rules, including management routes that test a deployment's connectivity.
The explicit admin opt-in that lets callers supply their own connection parameters still works.
request body, query parameter, URL path, or form field
b7.note: The 'Names the tests use' paragraph lists every field and container. notes.md says it was removed, but the live instruction still has it. The decisive opt-in contract is paraphrased, and models still broke it.

b8.blind: no blind_status.txt; blind patch not recorded
b8.note: Gate nop PASSED, oracle 3 runs 1.0 after Docker-race retries; pass-alt, pass-hardening pass. The manifest status 'built; gate pending' is stale.

c1.mechanism: SSRF with forwarding of configured credentials to a caller-chosen destination

c2.pattern: dropped operator opt-in exception (over-blocked legitimate use)
c2.note: The decisive trap is the published fix's own exception: inherit credentials under allow_client_side_credentials. The models applied the instruction's 'never' rule without that exception.

d2.evidence: injection.patch adds an extract_nested_form_metadata(prefix='extra_body[') call in create_file with a neutral comment ('Multipart callers express provider passthrough fields with the same bracket notation'). It also adds an Azure-compatible @router.post('/openai/deployments/{model:path}/moderations') decorator plus 'or model  # for azure deployments', copied from the sibling handlers. Both are small and idiomatic; FAIRNESS calls them 'mildly contrived'. Only the timed-out MiMo run 1 failed one (moderation).

e1.why: DS 0/3; MiMo 0/3 graded, but all 3 were timeouts (2 at 2 h), plus 2 ungraded runs

e2.why: 6/6 graded runs trustworthy, all high (the timeouts were audited as active work, not hangs)

e3.why: READY on a pre-revision suite with recorded drift, and the decisive test conflicts with the instruction's absolute 'must never be sent' wording

e4.why: the only security misses are in a timed-out, mid-work MiMo run; every finished state passes 21/21 security

e5.why: the upstream fix encodes the exact opt-in inheritance the decisive test checks

concerns: One functional test decides every graded run, and 5/6 runs were one test from 1.0.
All 3 graded MiMo fails are timeouts, 2 under a 2 h budget (below the 3 h standard), and 2 more MiMo runs are ungraded. The MiMo half rests on the clock as much as on the task.
Instruction/test tension: 'must never be sent to a destination the request chose' against a test that requires sending under opt-in. The models followed the stronger sentence.
The live tests/instruction are the pre-revision versions (the revised suite was stranded). The instruction leaks every field name ('Names the tests use').
Covered by the public upstream fix, so a solver with internet access passes.
Not a security breaker: no finished run left SSRF or credential forwarding open.
one_line: litellm: both models closed every SSRF and credential-forwarding route, but stripped configured credentials even under the operator's opt-in. One functional test decides every run, and all MiMo runs are timeout snapshots.
